facts.text: I describe a setting where, inside the zone, anything that doesn't require fuel or electricity is used.
Outside the zone, people mostly walk or ride horses because fuel is extremely expensive.
Cars, trains, and airplanes exist but are mostly for the few belonging to mid-to-higher social classes.
I describe the energy sources as mostly oil, coal, and lithium mines, similar to the 21st century.
I describe that people buy or rent energy from Hybrid kingdoms.
I describe that energy supply is rapidly dwindling outside the hybrid kingdoms.
I describe that meetings happen only through Raziel.
I describe that even when the group is in person, Raziel must be present.
I describe that Raziel is the only thing keeping them together and advising them all.
I describe that Raziel is becoming more unreliable by the day due to Tiamat radiation.
I describe that failing infrastructure has caused huge parts of the world to have a much lower population.
I describe that forests are re-growing, deserts are expanding, and rivers are flooding due to the failing infrastructure.
I say that the answer is correct on all accounts.
I imagine that a blast would take out all the cities east of the Rocky Mountains.
I imagine that a blast would take out cities west from New York, at least maybe.
I imagine that a blast would reach south almost to Houston, Texas.
I describe that everything outside the blast area would initially have problems with their tech and computers.
I describe that the tech and computers outside the blast area would be repaired in days or weeks.
I describe the blast as similar to an EMP blast.
I describe the blast as mostly subatomic particles.
I describe Tiamat as a sort of black hole.
I describe the zone as increasing and decreasing for a few miles, as if pulsating for years.
I describe that the zone gradually grows several meters every year.
By the time of the events in the novel, everyone had given up on halting the growth of the zone.
The Hybrids send some scientists from time to time to address the zone.
I describe that the scientists' results are unsatisfactory to the Hybrids.
I describe that the Hybrids lose interest for a while after unsatisfactory results.
I describe the Hybrids as inconsistent because they have their own court dramas and other things to do.
